From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Subject: Re: RFI: containment & egress controls for inference workloads

All — drafting technical content below, please edit for customer tone. I attached a sketched layout (inference-zone-containment-diagram.png) and a concise egress-policy spreadsheet. Key points: 

1) Isolation model (summary)
- Hardware tenancy: physical GPU pools are partitionable into Dedicated (tenant-exclusive) and Shared (multi-tenant) modes. Dedicated pools use strict hypervisor-level and driver isolation; Shared pools run tenant workloads in isolated containers with enforced cgroups and strict seccomp profiles.
- Process and memory separation: each model runtime is launched in a distinct container/process namespace; KV caches are namespaced per-model-instance and backed by ephemeral encrypted RAM or memory-mapped files that are zeroed on tear-down.
- KV cache exposure mitigations: cache namespaces are keyed by tenant+model-version; runtime checks reject keys without matching tenant assertion. Observability export sanitizes cached prefixes; raw cache dumps are never emitted to telemetry streams.

2) Failure containment and fallback behavior
- Zone concept: inference-zone (compute layer), control-plane-zone (orchestrator/route control), customer-edge-zone (VPC peering or private endpoint). Each zone has independent failure domains (AZ, rack, host).
- On host-level failure: requests routed to remaining hosts in same inference-zone; kernel-level isolation prevents memory/handle leakage.
- On zone-level (>30s) outage: smart-routing directs traffic to pre-provisioned fallback pools (either regional Dedicated pools or verified open-model low-cost variants) based on customer policy (latency-first vs data-residency-first). Fallback never exposes customer data across tenants.
- Rollback & canary: we support canary weightings and immediate circuit-breaker to prevent blended failures from propagating.

3) Egress controls and networking
- Outbound model updates and telemetry go over mTLS-authenticated private endpoints; we offer options: (a) BGP-managed interconnect with explicit route filters at peering, (b) NAT egress with strict allow-listing, (c) customer-managed private link (VPC endpoints).
- By default we recommend private endpoints with route filters for regulated customers; BGP interconnect is available for high-throughput customers with prefix filters and per-prefix route-maps.
- Firewall policy: deny-by-default inbound; outbound egress only to allowed IP ranges/DNS names. We publish an egress CIDR set for transparency and maintenance windows.

4) Telemetry and post-incident analysis
- Per-request trace id, token-level cost, host id, model variant, and KV-namespace id are recorded. Sensitive artifacts (full prompts) are redacted for hosted/shared modes by default; customers can opt-in for additional retention in Dedicated with contractual controls.
- Audit logs (KMS access, deployment rollouts, network policy changes) are retained per customer retention SLA and available via private log delivery.

I'll attach the diagram and egress matrix. Olga — can you own the customer-facing summary and threat-model bullets?

Attachments: inference-zone-containment-diagram.png; egress-policy-matrix.xlsx

Alice — attached are the deliverables for your architecture review: a one-page diagram, a short narrative, and a policy matrix. Highlights up front: 

- Tenant separation: Dedicated pools provide physical GPU isolation; Shared pools use process/container isolation and KV namespace enforcement.
- KV cache leakage: prevented by namespacing and runtime assertion checks; telemetry pipelines redact cached content before export.
- Failure containment: failures are contained within inference-zones; cross-zone fallback is controlled by explicit customer policy (latency vs residency).
- Egress: private endpoints recommended; BGP interconnect available with route filters; published egress CIDRs and allow-lists maintained with change notices.
- Telemetry: per-request trace ids and host metadata; raw prompts redacted unless contractually retained for Dedicated with strict controls.

Please find the attachments: inference-zone-containment-diagram.png, egress-policy-matrix.xlsx, rfi-cover-note.odt. Two quick asks: confirm whether you want BGP interconnect options surfaced in the RFP binder, and whether telemetry with raw prompt retention is allowed for a small set of sandbox workloads.
